subject.title: RFC: Consolidate turn execution behind a TurnEngine boundary

question: Should OpenClaw extend the RuntimePlan/Harness V2 finalization work with a canonical observable turn boundary, or keep the existing internal lifecycle boundaries without introducing a new `TurnEngine`/`replies` facade?
rationale: The proposal changes the long-term owner boundary across channel handlers, embedded runners, provider adapters, event delivery, and tests; source overlap alone cannot establish that this additional public/internal abstraction is desired.

options.title: Fold a scoped boundary into the existing RFC
options.body: Add only a maintainer-defined observable turn contract to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72072, preserving RuntimePlan and Harness V2 as the canonical lifecycle owners.

options.title: Keep current boundaries
options.body: Decline the new facade and continue the existing extraction roadmap without introducing a second top-level turn-execution API.

recommendation.title: Fold a scoped boundary into the existing RFC
recommendation.body: Add only a maintainer-defined observable turn contract to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72072, preserving RuntimePlan and Harness V2 as the canonical lifecycle owners.

likelyOwner.reason: They currently authored the overlapping RuntimePlan/Harness V2 finalization roadmap and are the clearest routing point for consolidating or rejecting this adjacent direction.
